title: feature-launch-slo-activation-cadet-playbook-90d
body:
Purpose & scope:
This is a lightweight, tactical 90-day "Cadet" playbook for product teams launching console features that require SLO alignment. The goal is to give a repeatable, cross-functional checklist and sprintable plan so launches get observable SLOs, guarded rollouts, and an immediate post-launch remediation path.

Why a "Cadet" playbook?
- Fast-moving feature teams need a pragmatic, low-friction way to adopt reliability guardrails without a heavy program kickoff.
- This playbook is explicitly prescriptive: daily/weekly tasks, templates for alerts/runbooks, and a small decision log for trade-offs.
- It treats SLO adoption as a 90-day experiment with clear pass/fail gates.

Audience:
- Product managers and engineering leads running console/rollout workstreams
- SRE partners (embedded or platform) who will sign off on SLOs and escalation paths
- Observability & monitoring owners who will configure metrics and alerts
- Customer support and solutions engineering for impact comms

High-level 90-day milestones (week ranges):
- W0 (pre-kickoff): Lightweight intake + risk classification
- W1–W2: Define SLOs, success metrics, and canary plan
- W3–W4: Implement telemetry, dashboards, and initial runbooks
- W5–W8: Canary, iterate on thresholds, and verify rollback paths
- W9–W13: Ramp/broad rollout, monitor burners, optimize cost/perf settings
- W14: Post-launch retro and SLO acceptance decision (finalize or iterate)

Roles & responsibilities (one-liners):
- PM (owner): drive decisions, stakeholder comms, prioritize bugs/tech debt during 90d
- Eng lead (owner): ensure instrumentation, deploy hooks for metrics, implement fallback behavior
- Eng-SRE (partner): propose SLO targets, own alerts/runbooks, lead oncall rotations for launch window
- Observability (owner): create dashboards, maintain query performance for high-cardinality metrics
- Platform (owner): capacity contingency and autoscale policies for dedicated/private customers
- Support & Solutions: prepare canned responses and escalation contact sheet

Intake checklist (W0):
- Fill the quick intake form: feature description, expected qps, traffic regions, customer tiers affected
- Classify risk: Low / Medium / High (criteria: stateful changes, dependency surface, customer-impact score)
- Attach PRD link, launch calendar date, and any external regulatory constraints
- Assign SRE partner and set initial 30/60/90 day meeting invites

SLO definition template (W1):
- Service name: <console-service>
- User-visible objective: e.g., "Console request success for saved searches"
- SLI: request_success_rate (200/2xx over 5m window) and p95 latency on interactive endpoints
- Target (initial): 99.5% availability for core path, p95 latency < 350ms for UI api
- Error budget policy: burn alerts at 50%, 80%, 100% with automatic gating on rollout percentage at 80% burn
- Measurement windows: rolling 7d primary, 1d short window for fast detection

Telemetry & instrumentation (W1–W3):
- Ensure each critical path emits: request id, route, latency ms, status code, customer_id (if tiered), and feature_flags
- Add synthetic checks for critical flows (login, open-dashboard, save-settings) scheduled every 1m for canary region
- Tagging convention to match billing/console dashboards: service=console, team=payments, feature=quick-filters

Dashboards & alerting (W2–W4):
- Dashboards: top-line SLO, burn rate, per-region latency, per-customer tier error spikes
- Alerts: set alert runbooks for both symptom (p95 high, success_rate drop) and cause (DB connection failures, cache evictions)
- Alert thresholds: Symptom alert at 1.5x p95 baseline or 2 sigma above noise; burn rate alarm at 50%/80%/100%
- Pager matrix: who to page at each threshold, and escalation chain for 1h unresolved incidents

Canary & rollout plan (W3–W8):
- Canary groups: internal-only -> beta customers -> 10% global -> 50% -> 100%
- Rollback triggers: sustained p95 > 2x baseline for 15m, or sustained success_rate < target - 1% for 30m, or error budget burn crossing 80%
- Automated gating: if burn rate alert >= 80% for 1h, pause rollout and reduce to prior stable tag
- Manual gating: PM/SRE decision at weekly cadence for ramping beyond 50%

Runbooks (W2–W5):
- Template items: symptom, likely causes, quick mitigation steps, rollback commands, runbook owner, playbook ticket link
- Example quick mitigation: flip feature_flag to previous value, throttle third-party calls, increase cache ttl for read-heavy endpoints
- Post-incident notes: short template to capture root-cause hypothesis, mitigations, and action items with owners

Decision log & trade-offs (ongoing):
- Keep a short chronologically ordered log (example entries below). This lives with the PRD and is referenced in the final SLO acceptance.
  - 2026-01-18: Set p95 latency target relaxed to 350ms from 200ms to avoid infra uplift; agreed temporary target for 90d.
  - 2026-02-03: Agreed to use per-region synthetic checks instead of global only.

Risk scenarios & mitigations (pre-mortem prompt):
- Sudden backend DB migrations cause 5x latency: mitigation: pre-schedule migration in low traffic window, enable rate-limiter, and have rollback snapshot ready.
- Third-party auth provider outage: mitigation: local caching of tokens and degraded read-only mode.
- Spike in telemetry cardinality: mitigation: short-circuit high-card metrics, switch to sampled traces, notify observability team to increase retention temporarily.

Success criteria at 90 days (W14):
- SLO either green or within agreed cadence of improvement plan (documented action items)
- Incident churn reduced to <= 1 Sev2 in the 90d window attributable to the feature
- Support volume for the feature <= projected threshold OR documented plan to address ongoing tickets
- Operational cost within 1.25x forecast for production footprint during launch window (if >1.25x, attach remediation plan)

Communications & stakeholder cadence:
- Daily stand for first week of canary with PM, Eng lead, SRE, and Observability (15m)
- Twice-weekly health sync while ramping 10%->50%
- Weekly summary emails to execs until 100% rollout
- Customer comms: pre-launch beta note, post-incident templated responses, SLA FAQs for enterprise customers

Templates to copy (location pointers):
- Intake form (Google form stub) -> CONFLUENCE link (placeholder)
- SLO declaration template -> (copy into product PRD)
- Minimal runbook template -> quick copy/paste for oncall rotations

Open questions / TODOs:
- Agree whether SLO measurement should treat transient 5xx from third-party as internal errors for burn calculation (SRE position: include; PM asks for exclusion for first 30d)
- Decide exact retention for high-res telemetry during ramp (cost trade-off)
- Confirm support escalation contact for APAC region (Lucy?)

Post-launch retro agenda (W14):
- Quick timeline of events and decision log review
- Metrics review vs. target (SLO burn, cost, support tickets)
- Actions: categorize into quick fixes (<2w), medium (2–8w), backlog (>8w). Assign owners and expected delivery dates.

Notes to cadets (tips from SREs):
- Start small on SLOs: pick 1–2 user journeys and measure them well rather than trying to do everything.
- Make fast rollback easier than perfect fixes. The simplest mitigation is usually feature_flag toggle.
- Maintain the decision log — it pays off when the execs ask why a target was chosen.

Appendix: quick checklist repeatable for each feature launch:
- Intake completed and risk class assigned
- SLO declared and baseline measured
- Synthetic checks running and dashboards created
- Runbooks written and assigned
- Canary plan documented with automated gates
- Support templates ready and comms scheduled
- 90-day retro invite on calendar

This is a working playbook — comments welcome. If this approach looks useful, we can turn the checklist into a lightweight Google Form + templated Confluence page for faster adoption across the console roadmap.

Unresolved: where to store the canonical decision log for long-lived features (Confluence vs. ephemeral PRD). Proposed in next sync: Confluence for long-term, PRD as source of truth for short-lived notes.

— Aisha (PM)
